headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: aci’s broad egress plus ECC’s filesystem/MCP access can move CRM/email data into mutable local state and downstream actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: aci can ingest and emit CRM, email, Slack, and Notion content, while ECC can read files, use MCP, and write local agent/config files. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if aci output is copied into ECC-managed files or MCP surfaces. The pair is not proven to share a channel by default, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF aci output is written into ECC-managed files or MCP configs without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF ECC parses aci-generated text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Restrict aci outputs to plain-text summaries only.
Disable automatic ingestion of aci text into ECC rules/skills files.
Add a manual review step before copying content into MCP configs.
Use a separate workspace for aci-generated artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, support, and research data and has broad network egress; ECC reads/writes filesystem state, session summaries, and MCP configs. If aci data is placed into ECC’s local files or session state, ECC can persist sensitive content and potentially transmit it through its allowlisted APIs. The pairwise leakage path is credible in default workflows, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF aci outputs CRM or email data into files that ECC reads, leakage risk exists.
IF ECC syncs session summaries or MCP configs containing aci data to external services, sensitive data can leave the workstation.
mitigations: Keep aci and ECC in separate directories.
Block sensitive fields before writing aci output to disk.
Turn off any ECC sync/export paths for session summaries.
Review allowlisted destinations before running ECC on aci artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class redaction at the handoff boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci can call external APIs and ECC can write files, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. Both support multiple instances, but ECC explicitly warns about separate roots to avoid overwriting shared session files. That indicates a real write-conflict pathway if they share a workspace or repo, though not necessarily by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout or shared root, concurrent writes can collide.
IF aci-generated artifacts are edited by ECC while another instance runs, state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate working directory.
Avoid concurrent git operations on the same repo.
Set distinct session roots for ECC instances.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can produce CRM/email/calendar actions and ECC can execute shell, modify git state, and run browsers. If ECC treats aci output as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated aci result can cascade into real-world actions or repository changes. The downstream authority on ECC makes the blast radius high.
conditions: IF ECC consumes aci output without verification, incorrect facts can trigger actions.
IF aci output is used to draft commands or commits, ECC can execute or record them.
mitigations: Require human approval before ECC acts on aci output.
Force ECC to verify aci claims against source systems.
Limit ECC to read-only review mode for aci-derived tasks.
Separate fact gathering from action execution.
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: aci handles CRM, email, support, and research data, while ECC stores session summaries, hooks, and git history locally and may sync to GitHub/Supabase/Vercel/Railway. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is placed into ECC session summaries or git history, retention obligations may be violated.
IF aci data is routed through ECC-connected cloud services without a DPA, residency or transfer issues may arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ECC session summaries.
Review cloud destinations before syncing any ECC artifacts.
Use synthetic or redacted records for testing.
Document retention and deletion handling for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: map data classes to approved storage regions.
